object_description: linear building volume with a roof crossing two axes
design_condition: The linear volume follows the north-south axis, uses the topographic difference to light basement spaces, and organizes earthworks to distinguish domestic areas from the more public park and courtyard.

positive.statement: The topographic difference allows natural lighting of the basement music rooms and aula and gives form to the adjacent district-facing facade.

position.rationale: Linear building surface anchors the basement zone low along the district-facing edge.

positive.statement: The rationality of the plan should be underlined.

position.rationale: Regular linear organization is read across the elongated top footprint and repeated elevations.

positive.statement: The concrete exoskeleton intelligently responds to modularity in plan while giving the facades a sculptural character.

position.rationale: Outer framed edges are visibly repeated around the linear volume.

positive.statement: The scale brought to the site is coherent and rigorously organized.

position.rationale: The long, compact footprint provides the sampled model’s scale reference.

positive.statement: The earthworks distinguish domestic spaces from the more public parts of the park and courtyard.

position.rationale: A low site-edge anchor represents the earthwork transition around the building.

negative.statement: The sports halls are not connected to the public staircase and are only accessible from the school, which impedes their use.

position.rationale: The eastern lower portion of the linear sample is used for the inaccessible sports zone.

negative.statement: The spatial qualities resulting from the rational plan do not correspond to the jury's expectations.

position.rationale: The critique concerns the overall repeated organization, anchored across the building mass.

negative.statement: The geometric system neglects the spatial gradation between the overall building scale and the scale of classrooms or subgroups.

position.rationale: A representative mid-building interior zone approximates classroom-scale relationships.

negative.statement: The composition seems to refer only to itself and has no link with the larger landscape or territorial structure.

position.rationale: The building edge is anchored where the sampled composition meets its implied landscape.

negative.statement: The predetermined functions of the subspaces work against the desired flexibility of use for a park of this size.

position.rationale: A lower interior zone represents the inflexible subdivision of park-related uses.
